newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth earnings rise in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth earnings rise in fourth quarter.

text.p: BellSouth Corp. reported Thursday a 12.3 percent rise in fourth quarter earnings before one-time items, continuing the strong growth the company has reaped from the robust Southern economy.
The Atlanta-based Baby Bell reported net income of $633 million, or 64 cents per share, compared with $564 million, or 57 a year ago, before one-time items and just beating Wall Street expectations.
"We're in an industry that's on fast forward," said Duane Ackerman, BellSouth chief executive officer. "The result of this (BellSouth) market focus is steady earnings growth," he said.
Special charges for workforce reductions a year ago of $725 million, or 73 cents per share, made for a total net loss of $161 million in 1995's fourth quarter, or 16 cents per share.
For the year BellSouth reported net income or $2.52 billion, or $2.53 per share, up from $2.23 billion or $2.24 per share, excluding one-time items in both periods.
"As usual their results looked very good," said Barry Sine, an industry analyst at brokers SBC Warburg. "I think their double digit earnings growth is sustainable."
In 1996 there was a $344 million gain on the sale of the paging business and, in 1995, $3.5 billion of charges, mostly a non-cash charge for an accounting change.

BellSouth said its access lines grew 4.7 percent in 1996, adding just over 1 million lines, the first regional Bell to do so. Its total lines to customers grew to 22.1 million, helped by a big second quarter boost from the Olympics.
Business access lines rose by 8.1 percent in the year.
Revenue from calling features like caller ID, voice mail and voice dialling grew rapidly to account for $1 billion in annual revenue in 1996. No year ago figure was given.
Total operating revenues rose 6 percent to $5.05 billion from $4.76 billion in the fourth quarter and operating expenses rose 5.7 percent, excluding year ago charges.

BellSouth's U.S. cellular customers jumped 26.9 percent in 1996 to 3.61 million but average revenue per customer slipped to $56 from $61. During the fourth quarter the company added 279,000 U.S. cellular customers and 765,000 for the year.
BellSouth stock closed $1.375 lower at $42.50 on the New York Stock Exchange as the broad market fell.
